title: Rigveda 1.172: To the Maruts
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.172: To the Maruts: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.172 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to the Maruts. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 136r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.172.1-3 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 4, varga 12); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 136r
translation.original_text:
1ci̱tro vo̍ 'stu̱ yāma̍ś ci̱tra ū̱tī su̍dānavaḥ | maru̍to̱ ahi̍bhānavaḥ ||
2ā̱re sā va̍ḥ sudānavo̱ maru̍ta ṛñja̱tī śaru̍ḥ | ā̱re aśmā̱ yam asya̍tha ||
3tṛ̱ṇa̱ska̱ndasya̱ nu viśa̱ḥ pari̍ vṛṅkta sudānavaḥ | ū̱rdhvān na̍ḥ karta jī̱vase̍ ||
translation.text:
1WONDERFUL let your coming be, wondrous with help, ye Bounteous Ones, Maruts, who gleam as serpents gleam.
2Far be from us, O Maruts, ye free givers, your impetuous shaft; Far from us be the stone ye hurl.
3O Bounteous Givers, touch ye not, O Maruts, Tr̥iṇaskanda's folk; Lift ye us up that we may live.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 136r (numbered 5r by the scribe) (OPenn image 137, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.171.3 ‹naḥ marutaḥ mṛḷayantu uta›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 136v (numbered 5v by the scribe), begins in RV 1.173.1 ‹veḥ arcāma tat vavṛdhānam›. Verses 1.172.1-3 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1citraḥ | vaḥ | astu | yāmaḥ | citraḥ | ūtī | su-dānavaḥ | marutaḥ | ahi-bhānavaḥ
2āre | sā | vaḥ | su-dānavaḥ | marutaḥ | ṛñjatī | śaruḥ | āre | aśmā | yam | asyatha
3tṛṇa-skandasya | nu | viśaḥ | pari | vṛṅkta | su-dānavaḥ | ūrdhvān | naḥ | katar | jīvase
